rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those whom they call upon” points to prophets, distinguishing them from powerless idols.
rows.anchor: والإشارة ب { أولئك الذين يدعون } إلى النبيئين لزيادة تمييزهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If invoked, prophets are answered and distress is removed; idols cannot remove distress or intercede, as experience showed.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : أولئك الذين إن دعوا يستجب لهم ويكشف عنهم الضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seeking clause is either circumstantial to the subject of “invoke” or explanatory of that clause.
rows.anchor: جملة { يبتغون } حال من ضمير { يدعون } أو بيان لجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wasīla means a lofty rank close to a great person, such as a king.
rows.anchor: والوسيلة : المرتبة العالية القريبة من عظيم كالملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parse makes “which of them is nearer” a partitive relative replacement: the nearest still seeks greater closeness through deeds.
rows.anchor: بدلا من ضمير { يبتغون } بدل بعض ، وتكون ( أي ) موصولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it replaces the whole seeking clause; “which” is interrogative and they seek to know who is nearest to God.
rows.anchor: بدلا من جملة { يبتغون إلى ربهم الوسيلة } ، و ( أي ) استفهامية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparative's omitted complement is “to their Lord,” supplied by context.
rows.anchor: وأقرب : اسم تفضيل ، ومتعلقه محذوف دل عليه السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear after hope signals reverent decorum: closeness to God increases awe, unlike polytheists who expect their partners' intercession.
rows.anchor: لا يزيدهم القرب من رضاه إلا إجلالا له وخوفا من غضبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause is a concluding summary: God's punishment merits vigilance by the rightly guided.
rows.anchor: وجملة { إن عذاب ربك كان محذورا } تذييل . ومعنى { كان محذورا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unbelieving towns face total destruction or worldly punitive retribution such as Badr's sword, humiliation, captivity, fear, and hunger.
rows.anchor: كل قرية مثل قريتهم في الشرك لا يعدوها عذاب الاستيصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended towns are those whose inhabitants disbelieve, as Hūd 11:117 and al-Qaṣaṣ 28:59 clarify.
rows.anchor: فالمراد : القرى الكافر أهلها لقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted qualifier “unbelieving” is familiar ellipsis; “every ship” in al-Kahf 18:79 means every sound ship from context.
rows.anchor: وحذف الصفة في مثل هذا معروف كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believing towns are not included in a universal claim that every town must vanish, which would conflict with other verses and the warning's purpose.
rows.anchor: وليس المقصود شمول ذلك القرى المؤمنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if every town must perish eventually as a created thing, that general rule would serve no purpose here.
rows.anchor: لما سلمنا أن في ذكر ذلك هنا فائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The before-Resurrection restriction heightens the warning, as Ṭā Hā 20:127 says next-life punishment is stronger and more lasting.
rows.anchor: والتقييد بكونه قبل يوم القيامة } زيادة في الإنذار والوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added min after negative in stresses exhaustive scope over the implied class of unbelieving towns, ensuring Mecca is included.
rows.anchor: و ( من ) مزيدة بعد ( إن ) النافية لتأكيد استغراق مدخولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The Book” means God's knowledge and prior decree, or revealed scriptures generically, including the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: والكتاب : مستعار لعلم الله وسابق تقديره ، فتعريفه للعهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masṭūr means written; the verb is illustrated by al-Qalam 68:1.
rows.anchor: والمسطور : المكتوب ، يقال : سطر الكتاب إذا كتبه سطورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse answers Quraysh's excuse: they demanded signs and arrogantly said a truthful prophet would produce requested miracles.
rows.anchor: كانوا يسألون النبي أن يأتيهم بآيات على حسب اقتراحهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joined to 17:58, God deferred punishment but withheld signs because earlier unbelievers rejected comparable signs.
rows.anchor: لعدم جدوى إرسال الآيات للأولين من قبيلهم في الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Prevent” literally means restraining an agent from an intended act, impossible for God; here it figuratively means diversion or non-occurrence.
rows.anchor: وهذا محال عن الله تعالى إذ لا مكره للقادر المختار . فالمنع هنا مستعار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Send” may be literal with “Our messenger” omitted and signs accompanying him, or figurative for producing signs, with bāʾ augmentative/objective.
rows.anchor: والإرسال يجوز أن يكون حقيقة فيكون مفعول { أن نرسل } محذوفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite “signs” are requested miracles, including al-Isrāʾ 17:90, al-Qaṣaṣ 28:48, and al-Anʿām 6:124.
rows.anchor: أي المعهودة من اقتراحهم كقولهم : { لن نؤمن لك حتى تفجر لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first an-clause is a verbal noun governed by omitted min, the preposition that منع regularly takes.
rows.anchor: و ( أن ) الأولى مفيدة مصدرا منصوبا على نزع الخافض ، وهو ( من )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second an-clause is the subject of “We prevented” in an exceptive-only construction.
rows.anchor: و ( أن ) الثانية مصدرها فاعل منعنا } على الاستثناء المفرغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing prevention to earlier denial is causal rhetoric: their denial caused the diversion.
rows.anchor: وإسناد المنع إلى تكذيب الأولين بالآيات مجاز عقلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows these rejecters will not believe, as earlier unbelievers did not; signs cannot cure entrenched disbelief, as Yūnus 10:96–97 says.
rows.anchor: أننا نعلم أنهم لا يؤمنون كما لم يؤمن من قبلهم من الكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More likely, this steadies believers and consoles the Prophet, saddened by his people's rejection.
rows.anchor: والأظهر أن هذا تثبيت لأفئدة المؤمنين لئلا يفتنهم الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The she-camel is circumstantial evidence: Thamūd received a sign, increased in disbelief, and punishment came swiftly.
rows.anchor: وجملة وآتينا ثمود الناقة } في محل الحال من ضمير الجلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mubṣira means plainly evident and illuminating, giving witnesses certainty, as al-Naml 27:13 says.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { مبصرة } واضحة الدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamūd is singled out because Arabs knew their story and saw nearby ruins on journeys between Mecca and Syria.
rows.anchor: ولأن آثار هلاكهم في بلاد العرب قريبة من أهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓalamū bihā can mean disbelief/wronging themselves or denial of sign status, as al-Naml 27:14 says.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون استعمل الظلم بمعنى الكفر لأنه ظلم النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ẓulm is literal: they wronged the innocent she-camel by hamstringing it; unlawful animal harm is injustice.
rows.anchor: أي ظلموا الناقة حين عقروها وهي لم تجن عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God withheld signs to preserve Quraysh, from whom many would enter Islam and spread it, honoring the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أراد الإبقاء عليهم ليدخل منهم في الإسلام كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Requested signs would have triggered the customary annihilation of obstinate rejecters; God preserved the community, as al-Anfāl 8:33 says.
rows.anchor: لأصروا على الكفر فحقت عليهم سنة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We send with signs” follows the same two grammatical analyses as “We prevented sending signs.”
rows.anchor: والقول في تعدية وما نرسل بالآيات } كالقول في { وما منعنا أن نرسل بالآيات }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takhwīf means making afraid; “only as warning” denies divine contest or hope of converting people already known not to believe.
rows.anchor: والقصر في قوله : { إلا تخويفا } لقصر الإرسال بالآيات على علة التخويف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reassures the Prophet amid denial and God's reprieve of persecuting enemies, recalling victory.
rows.anchor: هذه تسلية للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم على حزنه من تكذيب قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God “your Lord” signals the Prophet's honor, care, and support, as al-Ṭūr 52:48 says.
rows.anchor: هذا القول مسوق مساق التكرمة للنبيء وتصبيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When We said to you” may coordinate with 17:59 or be parenthetical.
rows.anchor: بالآيات ( الإسراء : 59 ) ويجوز أن تكون معترضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When” depends on omitted “remember”: repeat the promise to be patient; dhikr reinstates remembered information.
rows.anchor: أي اذكر إذ قلنا لك كلاما هو وعد بالصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Encompassing people themselves means domination; past tense assures imminent fulfillment, perhaps alluding to land shrinking in al-Raʿd 13:41.
rows.anchor: تعين أنها مستعملة في معنى الغلبة ، كما في قوله تعالى : { وظنوا أنهم أحيط بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should not grieve over their slander: God will take vengeance.
rows.anchor: فلا تحزن لافترائهم وتطاولهم فسننتقم منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is also described as coordinated with 17:59, with intervening material parenthetical.
rows.anchor: عطف على جملة { وما منعنا أن نرسل بالآيات ( الإسراء : 59 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruʾyā usually means a sleep dream but may mean eyewitness vision; Ibn ʿAbbās reportedly takes it as the Prophet's eye-vision on the Night Journey.
rows.anchor: كما نقل عن ابن عباس في هذه الآية ، قال : هي رؤيا عين

rows.speaker: عائشة ومعاوية وسبعة من التابعين
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhī reports the eye-vision as the view of ʿĀʾisha, Muʿāwiya, and seven named Successors.
rows.anchor: رواه الترمذي وقال : إنه قول عائشة ومعاوية وسبعة من التابعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the Prophet saw Jerusalem and accurately described it on the Night Journey, along with a caravan and its travelers.
rows.anchor: وتأولها جماعة أنها ما رآه ليلة أسري به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says he dreamed of entering Mecca at al-Ḥudaybiyya; being turned back confused some Muslims, but they entered the next year.
rows.anchor: وقيل : رأى أنه يدخل مكة في سنة الحديبية فرده المشركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view is a sleep vision of Quraysh leaders' deaths at Badr, shown to the Prophet in Mecca; prophetic dreams are revelation.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هي رؤيا مصارع صناديد قريش في بدر أريها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitna means disturbed judgment/disordered life or repeated unbearable punishment, as al-Burūj 85:10 and al-Dhāriyāt 51:13 say.
rows.anchor: والفتنة : اضطراب الرأي واختلال نظام العيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier vision interpretations further estranged polytheists from faith; on the Badr view, sword-punishment itself was the trial.
rows.anchor: أنها سبب فتنة المشركين بازدياد بعدهم عن الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cursed tree is zaqqūm, linked to al-Ṣāffāt 37:64–66, al-Dukhān 44:43–44, and al-Wāqiʿa 56:51–52.
rows.anchor: { والشجرة } عطف على الرؤيا ، أي ما جعلنا ذكر الشجرة الملعونة

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: Abū Jahl mocked that fire burns stone but a tree in hell would survive; God can create a tree the fire cannot consume.
rows.anchor: روي أن أبا جهل قال : زعم صاحبكم أن نار جهنم تحرق الحجر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأصحابه
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and companions transmit the mockery report in occasion-of-revelation works and al-Ṭabarī's tafsīr.
rows.anchor: وهذا مروي عن ابن عباس وأصحابه في أسباب النزول

rows.speaker: ابن الزبعرى
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zibʿarāʾ said zaqqūm meant dates with butter in Yemeni usage; Abū Jahl served it mockingly.
rows.anchor: وروي أن ابن الزبعرى قال : الزقوم التمر بالزبد بلغة اليمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the dates-and-butter view, mentioning the tree—not the tree itself—is the trial; “its mention” is understood from “cursed in the Qur'an.”
rows.anchor: أن ذكرها كان سبب فتنة بحذف مضاف وهو ذكر بقرينة قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Present verbs imply recurring warning and renewed rebellion: each new warning brings greater defiance.
rows.anchor: وقد اختير الفعل المضارع في نخوفهم } و { يزيدهم } لاقتضائه تكرر التخويف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Great” metaphorically means strong and intense rebellion, as at al-Baqara 2:217.
rows.anchor: والكبير : مستعار لمعنى الشديد القوى في نوع الطغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Adam story consoles the Prophet by recalling prophetic opposition and envy from Iblīs onward, even as some acknowledge prophets' merit as angels did Adam.
rows.anchor: والمقصود من هذا هو تذكير النبي بما لقي الأنبياء قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers align with the angelic camp and unbelievers with Satan's, as 17:63's “whoever follows you” signals.
rows.anchor: فلفريق الملائكة المؤمنون ولفريق الشيطان الكافرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The detailed Adam story and wording were already treated in al-Baqara and following passages.
rows.anchor: وتفسير قصة آدم وبيان كلماتها مضى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblīs's question about prostrating is denial: he will not do it.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام في أأسجد } إنكار ، أي لا يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speech is explanatory: the exception only said Iblīs did not prostrate, raising why; the reply reveals ignorant, arrogant disobedience.
rows.anchor: استثناء إبليس من حكم السجود لم يفد أكثر من عدم السجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Clay” is circumstantial to the relative pronoun, meaning Adam was created from clay; naming the earthly element magnifies Iblīs's contempt.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { طينا } حال من اسم الموصول ، أي الذي خلقته في حال كونه طينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Have you considered?” appositionally expands Iblīs's rejection, again denying Adam's preference and implying malice toward descendants.
rows.anchor: وجملة { قال أرأيتك } بدل اشتمال من جملة { أأسجد لمن خلقت طينا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Araytaka opens an important question (“tell me what you think”), combining interrogative, raʾā (“know”), subject suffix, and addressee kāf.
rows.anchor: تركيب يفتتح بها الكلام الذي يراد تحقيقه والاهتمام به

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: Basran grammarians treat the kāf in araytaka as emphatic address.
rows.anchor: وهذه الكاف عند البصريين تأكيد لمعنى الخطاب

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats kāf as an accusative pronoun (“see yourself”); Ibn ʿĀshūr says this better fits usage.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : الكاف ضمير نصب ، والتركيب : أرأيت نفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Anʿām 6:40 and Ṭarafa's “aramī” (“I see myself”) illustrate the construction.
rows.anchor: فما لي أراني وابن عمي مالكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative is contemptuous, as in al-Anbiyāʾ 21:36.
rows.anchor: واسم الإشارة مستعمل في التحقير ، كقوله تعالى : أهذا الذي يذكر آلهتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional is an oath: lām introduces an omitted oath, while the report functions as a wish, like Ṣād 38:79.
rows.anchor: واللام موطئة للقسم المحذوف مع الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's “Go” answers Iblīs's request for delay, separated as in Qur'anic dialogue and al-Baqara 2:30.
rows.anchor: جواب من الله تعالى عن سؤال إبليس التأخير إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Go” means continue the intended scheme, not depart; the imperative grants leave, illustrated by a Nabhānī poem.
rows.anchor: والذهاب ليس مرادا به الانصراف بل هو مستعمل في الاستمرار على العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Whoever follows you” follows from permission and rebuke, as in Ṭā Hā 20:97.
rows.anchor: تفريع على التسوية والزجر كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jazāʾ is a verbal noun for recompense, used as a passive noun like khalq for created thing.
rows.anchor: والجزاء : مصدر جزاه على عمل ، أي أعطاه عن عمله عوضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawfūr is the passive participle of wafara, “make abundant.”
rows.anchor: والموفور : اسم مفعول من وفره إذا كثره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating jazāʾ emphasizes the threat and improves flow; it frames a circumstantial phrase meaning undiminished recompense.
rows.anchor: وأعيد جزاء } للتأكيد ، اهتماما وفصاحة ، كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istifzāz means making light and unsettled through intense urging.
rows.anchor: والاستفزاز : طلب الفز ، وهو الخفة والانزعاج وترك التثاقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Voice” means speech and metaphorically Satan's whisper in hearts; it may belong to the army simile.
rows.anchor: والصوت : يطلق على الكلام كثيرا ، لأن الكلام صوت من الفم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ijlāb is mustering and driving an army, from jalaba (“uproar”), as a commander calls troops to raid.
rows.anchor: والإجلاب : جمع الجيش وسوقه ، مشتق من الجلبة بفتحتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayl is a collective noun for horses and means cavalry in context; the Prophetic call “O God's cavalry, mount” illustrates it.
rows.anchor: والخيل : اسم جمع الفرس . والمراد به عند ذكر ما يدل على الجيش الفرسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's power to mislead is pictured as a commander mobilizing cavalry and foot soldiers; “voice” may be the army's call.
rows.anchor: وهو تمثيل لحال صرف قوته ومقدرته على الإضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rajl is a collective noun for men; Arab armies combined foot soldiers with swords and cavalry shooting arrows before close combat.
rows.anchor: والرجل : اسم جمع الرجال كصحب

rows.speaker: أنيف بن زبان النبهاني
rows.claim: Anīf ibn Zabān's poem depicts infantry under horses shooting arrows before armies meet with swords.
rows.anchor: وتحت نحور الخيل حرشف رجلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image means gathering every temptation and whispering device against Adam's descendants like a large invading army.
rows.anchor: أجمع لمن اتبعك من ذرية آدم وسائل الفتنة والوسوسة

rows.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ reads rajil with kasra on jīm, a dialect form of rajul with ḍamma; it generically means foot soldiers.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حفص عن عاصم { ورجلك } بكسر الجيم ، وهو لغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in “with your cavalry” reinforces object attachment or reflects ijlab carrying the meaning “invade them.”
rows.anchor: والباء في { بخيلك } إما لتأكيد لصوق الفعل لمفعوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sharing wealth means allocating livestock and harvest shares to idols, as al-Anʿām 6:136 describes.
rows.anchor: أن يكون للشيطان نصيب في أموالهم وهي أنعامهم وزروعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sharing children includes infanticide, children conceived in fornication, and names linking children to idols.
rows.anchor: مثل تسويله لهم أن يئدوا أولادهم وأن يستولدوهم من الزنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan promises parents that dedication to idols averts bereavement or illness, idols intercede or grant victory, no afterlife punishment exists, and sins yield pleasures.
rows.anchor: أعطهم المواعيد بحصول ما يرغبونه كما يسول لهم بأنهم إن جعلوا أولادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of “promise them” is omitted for generality; context supplies desirable things, and future promises delay a liar's exposure.
rows.anchor: وحذف مفعول { وعدهم } للتعميم في الموعود به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghurūr is presenting harmful things as attractive; compare Āl ʿImrān 3:196 and al-Anʿām 6:112.
rows.anchor: والغرور : إظهار الشيء المكروه في صورة المحبوب الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Promises are false beliefs that never materialize or pleasures that eventuate in harm; al-Ghazālī expands this in his Book of Delusion.
rows.anchor: إما باطل لا يقع ، مثل ما يسوله للناس من العقائد الفاسدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such pleasures satisfy anger or appetite and favor immediate gratification over afterlife, always bringing or leading to harm.
rows.anchor: قضاء دواعي الغضب والشهوة ومحبة العاجل دون تفكير في الآجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assurance about God's servants completes the reply: some descendants will not follow Satan, prompting the question of their protection.
rows.anchor: لا يتبع إبليس فلا يحتنكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “My servants” means those wholly devoted to God, excluding idol- and jinn-worshippers.
rows.anchor: تمحضوا لعبودية الله تعالى كما تدل عليه الإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's sufficiency as guardian points to reliance on and refuge in Him, by which He protects them from Satan.
rows.anchor: أنهم توكلوا على الله واستعاذوا به من الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Degrees of reliance and escape from Satan's grasp match believers' degrees of obedience; this is the Sunni position.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا التوكل مراتب من الانفلات عن احتناك الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Denied authority is lasting rule making people Satan's subjects; others may be tempted but return to good and retain monotheism.
rows.anchor: هو الحكم المستمر بحيث يكونون رعيته ومن جنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This parallels al-Naḥl 16:99–100: Satan lacks authority over believers who rely on God, but rules those who ally with him.
rows.anchor: إنه ليس له سلطان على الذين آمنوا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A believer never allies with Satan but may be deceived by whispers, cursing Satan for major sins; greater deception means greater proximity to Satan's authority.
rows.anchor: فالمؤمن لا يتولى الشيطان أبدا ولكنه قد ينخدع لوسواسه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the Farewell Pilgrimage sermon, the Prophet said Satan despaired of being worshipped in their land but accepted lesser acts people deemed insignificant.
rows.anchor: إن الشيطان قد يئس أن يعبد في بلدكم هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Your Lord suffices as guardian” may complete the rebuke to Satan or be a parenthesis addressing the Prophet; meaning is the same.
rows.anchor: تكملة لتوبيخ الشيطان ، فيكون كاف الخطاب ضمير الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage returns to evidence of God's unique control, combining benefits with proof of worldly order and human mastery; it resembles 17:11.
rows.anchor: عود إلى تقرير أدلة الانفراد بالتصريف في العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to polytheists: after rescue on land they turn from God to idols, while in distress they call only Him.
rows.anchor: والخطاب لجماعة المشركين كما يقتضيه قوله عقبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Your Lord,” a title of care and authority, captures attention toward an important divine act.
rows.anchor: لاستدعاء إقبال السامعين على الخبر المؤذن بأهميته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominal clause and definite terms convey permanence and exclusivity: God alone continually drives ships.
rows.anchor: وجيء بالجملة الإسمية لدلالتها على الدوام والثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present relative verb signals renewal; the concise sentence compresses many meanings in an inimitable form.
rows.anchor: وجيء بالصلة فعلا مضارعا للدلالة على تكرر ذلك وتحدده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yuzjī means to drive slowly, like urging a heavily laden animal.
rows.anchor: ويزجي : يسوق سوقا بطيئا شبه تسخير الفلك للسير في الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fulk is plural here; baḥr is abundant water including the Euphrates and Tigris, as at al-Baqara 2:164.
rows.anchor: والفلك هنا جمع لا مفرد . والبحر : الماء الكثير فيشمل الأنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God's favor means seeking livelihood through trade, as at al-Baqara 2:198.
rows.anchor: والابتغاء : الطلب . والفضل : الرزق ، أي للتجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This universal favor benefits Yemenis, Iraqis, and others though Meccans did not use sea travel.
rows.anchor: لأن أهل مكة ما كانوا ينتفعون بركوب البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their conduct proves they recognize God's sole control, then their reversal after danger passes is astonishing.
rows.anchor: أعقبه بدليل آخر من أحوالهم المتضمنة إقرارهم بانفراده بالتصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sea-distress statement functions as proof and binding argument, not literal report.
rows.anchor: خبر مستعمل في التقرير وإلزام الحجة إذ لا يخبر أحد عن فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rescue-and-turning statement expresses amazement and rebuke.
rows.anchor: خبر مستعمل في التعجيب والتوبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harm at sea means fear of imminent drowning, which distresses the soul.
rows.anchor: وضر البحر : هو الإشراف على الغرق ؛ لأنه يزعج النفوس خوفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍalla does not mean idols vanish: the names of those habitually invoked disappear from people's tongues in crisis.
rows.anchor: فلا تدعونهم ، وذلك بقرينة ذكر الدعاء هنا الذي متعلقه اللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception can be connected because God's name, like idols' names, is sometimes on their tongues.
rows.anchor: والاستثناء من عموم الموصول ، لأن اسم الله مما يجري على ألسنتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “those invoked” means idols; in distress they call God, as al-ʿAnkabūt 29:65 says. This better fits “you turned away.”
rows.anchor: ولعل هذا الوجه أرجح لأنه أنسب بقوله : أعرضتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition “to” embeds “brought and delivered you” to land.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { إلى البر } عدي بحرف ( إلى ) لتضمين { نجاكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Mankind is ungrateful” is a parenthetic conclusion; kafūr is intensive and al-insān generic.
rows.anchor: وجملة { وكان الإنسان كفورا } اعتراض وتذييل لزيادة التعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic may conventionally mean most people, especially polytheists, whose ingratitude culminates in associating others with the benefactor.
rows.anchor: فهذا الاستغراق يجوز أن يكون استغراقا عرفيا بحمله على غالب نوع الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, people are never wholly free of repeated ingratitude through forgetfulness or attributing gifts to causes and imagined benefactors.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الاستغراق حقيقيا ، أي كان نوع الإنسان كفورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense signals ingrained ingratitude because senses distract people from reflecting beyond the perceptible world.
rows.anchor: وذكر فعل ( كان ) إشارة إلى أن الكفران مستقر في جبلة هذا الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Comfort becomes habitual and is forgotten, while hardship revives remembrance; compare Fuṣṣilat 41:51.
rows.anchor: وهو معنى قوله تعالى : { وإذا أنعمنا على الإنسان أعرض ونأى بجانبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since gratitude requires memory, religious practice teaches recalling blessings, as Ibrāhīm 14:5 says.
rows.anchor: من آداب النفس في الشريعة تذكيرها بنعم الله ، قال تعالى : وذكرهم بأيام الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat follows their abandonment of gratitude and return to disbelief; intervening material is parenthetical.
rows.anchor: وفرع الاستفهام التوبيخي على إعراضهم عن الشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khasf is the earth's surface overturning into its interior in an earthquake; compare al-Naḥl 16:45.
rows.anchor: والخسف : انقلاب ظاهر الأرض في باطنها من الزلزال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Land's safety is an overlooked blessing: an earthquake offers no escape, so people should remember safety while recognizing land's risks.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا تنبيه على أن السلامة في البر نعمة عظيمة تنسونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is reproachful and denies that they can feel secure.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام بقوله : أفأمنتم } إنكاري وتوبيخي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Side of the land” means the shore reached; danger can strike on arrival, showing land and sea equally subject to God's power.
rows.anchor: وجعل البر جانبا لإرادة الشق الذي ينجيهم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive is explicative, and bāʾ in “make you sink” marks accompaniment.
rows.anchor: وإضافة الجانب إلى البر إضافة بيانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥāṣib is a stoning storm, metaphorically hail like stones; alternatively it means a bearer of pebbles in a nisba-like form.
rows.anchor: والحاصب : الرامي بالحصباء ، وهي الحجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wakīl means defender or claimant; nobody could argue for them or seek compensation as kin might after land disaster.
rows.anchor: أي لا تجدوا لأنفسكم من يجادلنا عنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Am is transitional with an omitted question: “rather, are you safe from returning to sea and facing destructive wind?”
rows.anchor: و ( أم ) عاطفة الاستفهام ، وهي للإضراب الانتقالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some derive tāra from a hamza softened in frequent use; others from wāw. Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers hamza, attested and commonly softened.
rows.anchor: قيل عينه همزة ثم خففت لكثرة الاستعمال . وقيل : هي واو . والأول أظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Make you return” means creating motives leading back to sea as prelude to drowning and retribution.
rows.anchor: معنى { أن يعيدكم } أن يوجد فيكم الدواعي إلى العود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāṣif means breaking; as a wind adjective it describes a storm wrecking ships and drowning people, like ʿāṣif in Yūnus 10:22.
rows.anchor: والقاصف : التي تقصف ، أي تكسر . وأصل القصف : الكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use singular al-rīḥ; Abū Jaʿfar reads plural al-riyāḥ.
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور { من الريح } بالإفراد . وقرأ أبو جعفر { من الرياح } بصيغة الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ gives cause and mā is a verbal noun: “because of your shirk.”
rows.anchor: والباء في { بما كفرتم } للسببية . و ( ما ) مصدرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma escalates the threat: after drowning no rescuer remains, though some drowning people are saved.
rows.anchor: و ( ثم ) للترتيب الرتبي كشأنها في عطفها الجمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabīʿ intensifies follower: one who pursues a claim or demands vengeance.
rows.anchor: والتبيع : مبالغة في التابع ، أي المتتبع غيره المطالب لاقتضاء شيء منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sea suits “avenger”: a tribe cannot reach the sea to pursue a wrongdoer, unlike in the land threat.
rows.anchor: فلو راموا الثأر لهم لركبوا البحر ليتابعوا آثار من ألحق بهم ضرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to implied drowning or to the mentioned wind and its assault.
rows.anchor: إما إلى الإغراق المفهوم من { يغرقكم } ، وإما إلى المذكور من إرسال القاصف وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use yāʾ for five verbs; Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read them with divine nūn, shifting person, while Abū Jaʿfar and Ruways read “you drown” with tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور ألفاظ { يخسف } و { يرسل } و { يعيدكم } و { فيرسل }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This parenthesis recalls God's favor to all and summarizes the preceding discourse; descriptions apply to humankind as a type.
rows.anchor: اعتراض جاء بمناسبة العبرة والمنة على المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The five favors are dignity, land transport, sea transport, good provisions, and superiority over many creatures.
rows.anchor: وقد جمعت الآية خمس منن : التكريم ، وتسخير المراكب في البر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dignity makes people precious rather than abject in appearance, cleanliness, dress, comfort, eating, foresight, self-awareness, knowledge, craft, and civilization.
rows.anchor: فإن جميع الحيوان لا يعرف النظافة ولا اللباس ولا ترفيه المضجع والمأكل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās illustrates dignity by people lifting food and water to their mouths with fingers or utensils, unlike animals.
rows.anchor: وقد مثل ابن عباس للتكريم بأن الإنسان يأكل بأصابعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Land transport means riding mounts that God subjected and taught people to use.
rows.anchor: والحمل : الوضع على المركب من الرواحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sea carrying means being inside a ship, a conventional metaphor from riding; God inspired ships, sails, and oars, as al-Ḥāqqa 69:11 says.
rows.anchor: وأما الحمل في البحر فهو الحصول في داخل السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good provisions include knowledge of appealing foods and benefits; humans eat more varied fare than animals.
rows.anchor: ألهم الإنسان أن يطعم ما يشاء مما يروق له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended superiority is observable: human reason and ingenuity allow mastery over earthly creatures.
rows.anchor: فالمراد به التفضيل المشاهد لأنه موضع الامتنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dignity concerns worth in itself; superiority concerns distinction through reason, judgment, knowledge, and sciences.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين التفضيل والتكريم بالعموم والخصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Comparison with unseen angels or jinn is not intended; revelation establishes rankings. Ibn ʿĀshūr rebukes al-Zamakhsharī for forcing Muʿtazilī polemic into the verse.
rows.anchor: فليست بمقصودة هنا وإنما تعرف بأدلة توقيفية من قبل الشريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Many” deliberately limits the claim: some creatures may equal or exceed humans; revelation explains what it does and silence should not be speculated about.
rows.anchor: مراد منه التقييد والاحتراز والتعليم الذي لا غرور فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite absolute object tafḍīlan conveys greatness: God favored humans greatly.
rows.anchor: في قوله : { تفضيلا } لإفادة ما في التنكير من التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage shifts from worldly threats at 17:66–69 to the Hereafter's warning and promise as a fresh opening.
rows.anchor: انتقال من غرض التهديد بعاجل العذاب في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though “day” could link human favor to its future consequence, Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers an independent start: omitted “remember” makes yawm an object, not adverb.
rows.anchor: فترجح أنه ابتداء مستأنف استئنافا ابتدائيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other parses make yawm built: a subject predicated by “whoever receives,” or an adverb of an omitted verb for people differing; al-Akhfash and Ibn Burhān allow an added fa unlike Sībawayh.
rows.anchor: وإما أن تكون فتحته فتحة بناء لإضافته اسم الزمان إلى الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An imām is what people follow; here it is the followed religion, true for believers and false for the misguided.
rows.anchor: والإمام : ما يؤتم به ، أي يعمل على مثل عمله أو سيرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nations are called as “community of Muhammad/Moses/Jesus,” other religions, or worshippers of idols.
rows.anchor: أن يدعى يا أمة فلان ويا أتباع فلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ marks the object of “call,” used with idioms such as calling by a kunya or slogan.
rows.anchor: والباء لتعدية فعل { ندعوا } لأنه يتعدى بالباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming people by leaders brings joy to guided followers and distress to followers of misleaders, who see their stations and fate.
rows.anchor: وفائدة ندائهم بمتبوعيهم التعجيل بالمسرة لاتباع الهداة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The right-hand record recipients detail the groups summoned by imāms.
rows.anchor: وفرع على هذا قوله : { فمن أوتي كتابه بيمينه } تفريع التفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Whoever receives” coordinates with implied “they receive their books,” meaning records of deeds.
rows.anchor: عطف على مقدر يقتضيه قوله : { ندعوا كل أناس بإمامهم } أي فيؤتون كتبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inspires the righteous to take the record in their right hand, signifying care and important work; compare al-Ḥāqqa 69:45 and the charity report.
rows.anchor: وتلك علامة عناية بالمأخوذ ، لأن اليمين يأخذ بها من يعزم عملا عظيما

rows.speaker: الشماخ
rows.claim: Al-Shammākh's poem shows ʿArāba receiving the banner of glory with his right hand.
rows.anchor: تلقاها عرابة باليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The damned receive their records in their left hands, as al-Ḥāqqa 69:25 says.
rows.anchor: وأما أهل الشقاوة فيؤتون كتبهم بشمائلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative singles out right-hand recipients as readers; reviewing good deeds and reward is joyful, while others are omitted here.
rows.anchor: للتنبيه على أنهم دون غيرهم يقرؤون كتابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Isrāʾ 17:13–14 supplies the contrast: each person's record is brought open and he is told to read.
rows.anchor: وورد في الآية التي قبلها في هذه السورة وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓulm means diminution, a metonymy from injustice's usual removal; reward is something people would wish increased, as al-Kahf 18:33 illustrates.
rows.anchor: والظلم مستعمل هنا بمعنى النقص كما في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatīl is the thread in a date-stone cleft, a proverb for a tiny amount, as in al-Nisāʾ 4:49.
rows.anchor: والفتيل : شبه الخيط تكون في شق النواة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “More astray in path” conveys comparison without deriving a comparative from aʿmā; Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers the longer path image for vividness, comparing the person's two states.
rows.anchor: فعدل عن اللفظ الوجيز إلى التركيب المطنب لما في الإطناب من تمثيل الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afterlife misguidance is worse because worldly guidance remained available through the Messenger and Qur'an, whereas the next-life state is inescapable and accompanies lasting torment.
rows.anchor: ووجه كون ضلاله في الآخرة أشد أن ضلاله في الدنيا كان في مكنته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second group contrasts with right-hand recipients; left-hand fate is implicit and blindness supplies another description.
rows.anchor: وعطف ومن كان في هذه أعمى } عطف القسيم على قسيمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “This” is worldly life; blindness there metaphorically means misguidance.
rows.anchor: والإشارة ب { هذه } إلى معلوم من المقام وهو الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blindness in the Hereafter metaphorically means confusion and mental disarray.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالعمى في الآخرة ما ينشأ عن العمى من الحيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿmā is a simple descriptor in both instances, not a comparative; the next phrase conveys intensity.
rows.anchor: ووصف { أعمى } في المرتين مراد به مجرد الوصف لا التفضيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh tried to entice the Prophet to praise their gods so they could reconcile and agree.
rows.anchor: حال طمعهم في أن يستنزلوا النبي لأن يقول قولا فيه حسن ذكر لآلهتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hidden third-person pronouns refer to Quraysh's leaders.
rows.anchor: وضمائر الغيبة مراد منها كفار قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from addressing them to addressing the Prophet marks a move from argument to divine favor and consolation.
rows.anchor: وغير الأسلوب من خطابهم في آيات ربكم الذي يزجي لكم الفلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitna is a harmful, unsettling trial that pressures strength and thought; compare al-Baqara 2:191.
rows.anchor: والفتن والفتون : معاملة يلحق منها ضر واضطراب النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Turn you from” embeds ṣarafa (“divert”), naming the attempt's aim; what was revealed is the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وعدي يفتنونك } بحرف ( عن ) لتضمينه معنى فعلل كان الفتن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best reading fits wording and prophetic infallibility: he was not tempted to comply.
rows.anchor: مع ملاحظة ما تقتضيه أدلة عصمة الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī collected other readings; some have weak chains and poor fit, while others strain the wording. Reports describe Quraysh asking not to be equated with marginal believers.
rows.anchor: وللمفسرين بضعة محامل أخرى لهذه الآية استقصاها القرطبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh reportedly asked not to be equated with Bilāl, ʿAmmār, Khabbāb, and Ṣuhayb, promising to listen if they were excluded and idols not disparaged.
rows.anchor: أن المشركين راودوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن لا يسويهم مع من يعدونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, “what We revealed” means the portion Quraysh wanted changed: verses honoring believers such as al-Anʿām 6:52 or verses disparaging idols.
rows.anchor: وهو ما فيه فضل المؤمنين مثل قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports show fabrication and narrowness, but the verse can be read to accommodate them without misleading readers.
rows.anchor: وسمات التخرص وضيق العطن في معنى الآية بحاق ألفاظها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's wish to draw Quraysh toward Islam may have led him to consider mildness, delay, or yielding the gathering to their elite, serving religion without loss to Muslims.
rows.anchor: إن رغبة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في اقترابهم من الإسلام وفي تأمين المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is God's favor in preserving the Prophet from error in judgment, strengthening believers, and making polytheists despair of concessions.
rows.anchor: فهذه الآية مسوقة مساق المن على النبي بعصمة الله إياه من الخطأ في الاجتهاد
